title: Gapped face complements have finite inner horn presentations
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, inner horns and quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $n\geq2$ and let $J\subseteq[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$. For $S\subseteq[n]$, let $\Delta^S\subseteq\Delta^n$ be the face consisting of those simplices whose vertex image is contained in $S$. Put $K_J=\bigcup_{q\in J}\Delta^{[n]\setminus\{q\}}$; equivalently its simplices are the monotone maps into $[n]$ whose images do not contain all of $J$. Suppose that there are $i<j<k$ in $[n]$ with $i,k\in J$ and $j\notin J$. Then there is a finite filtration $K_J=L_0\subseteq L_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq L_t=\Delta^n$ by simplicial subsets such that every inclusion $L_{h-1}\hookrightarrow L_h$ is a pushout of an inner horn inclusion $\Lambda^{d_h}_{a_h}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{d_h}$ with $d_h\geq2$ and $0<a_h<d_h$. Pushout here means pushout in every simplicial degree in sets, with the induced simplicial operators. Consequently, for every quasicategory $Q$, every simplicial map $K_J\to Q$ extends to a simplicial map $\Delta^n\to Q$, with its restriction to $K_J$ exactly the given map.

source.place: HTT Lemma 4.4.5.8 and its finite horn-filtration proof, printed pp.305-306 (PDF pp.322-323); read online, archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag

proof.text: Use the standard-simplex convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A simplex $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$ belongs to $\Delta^S$ exactly when its image is contained in $S$. Thus it belongs to $K_J$ exactly when its image omits a vertex of $J$. All unions below are degreewise unions, which are closed under precomposition and hence are simplicial subsets. In particular these membership criteria apply to degenerate simplices as well as injective ones; no nondegenerate-simplex decomposition theorem is needed.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.8, description of K; direct image-set formulation. Printed pp.305-306 (PDF page indices 322-323), read online; archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Fix the given gap $i<j<k$. Let $P$ be the finite collection of subsets $T\subseteq[n]$ containing $J\cup\{j\}$. List its elements as $T_1,\ldots,T_t$ in increasing cardinality, with any order among sets of equal cardinality. A proper subset in $P$ therefore occurs earlier. Put $L_0=K_J$ and $L_h=K_J\cup\bigcup_{b\leq h}\Delta^{T_b}$. These are increasing simplicial subsets by step 1. The full set $[n]$ is the unique largest element of $P$, so $T_t=[n]$ and $L_t=\Delta^n$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.8 proof, P, its linear ordering and K(h). Printed pp.305-306 (PDF page indices 322-323), read online; archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: At stage $h$, write $T=T_h=\{v_0<\cdots<v_d\}$ and let $a$ be the index of $j$ in this list. Since $T$ contains $i,j,k$, one has $d\geq2$ and $0<a<d$. For any $v\in T$ different from $j$, the face on $T\setminus\{v\}$ is already in $L_{h-1}$: if $v\in J$, it omits a vertex of $J$ and lies in $K_J$; if $v\notin J$, it still contains $J\cup\{j\}$, belongs to $P$, and has smaller cardinality than $T$, so was attached earlier. This uses only the face membership criterion of step 1 and the ordering of step 2.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.8 proof, the faces in the upper-left inner horn of its pushout square. Printed pp.305-306 (PDF page indices 322-323), read online; archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Using the standard-simplex face membership convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the distinguished face $F=T\setminus\{j\}$ is absent from $L_{h-1}$. Indeed $j\notin J$, so $J\subseteq F$, and the injective simplex on $F$ does not belong to $K_J$. If it belonged to an earlier face $\Delta^{T_b}$, then $F\subseteq T_b$. But $j\in T_b$, hence $T=F\cup\{j\}\subseteq T_b$, while $b<h$ implies $|T_b|\leq|T|$. This forces $T_b=T$, contradicting distinctness of the enumeration. The simplex on $T$ is absent too, since its restriction to $F$ would otherwise be present. This is the entire exclusion argument; it invokes no lifting or anodyne-saturation lemma.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.8 proof, verification that the omitted j-face has not already been attached. Printed pp.305-306 (PDF page indices 322-323), read online; archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Identify $\Delta^d$ with the face $\Delta^T$ by the increasing bijection $[d]\to T$. We claim that its intersection with $L_{h-1}$ is exactly $\Lambda_a^d$. A simplex in the horn omits some $v\in T$ other than $j$, so lies in the face already present by step 3. Conversely, if its image omits no vertex of $T$ other than possibly $j$, that image is $F$ or $T$. Such a simplex cannot lie in $L_{h-1}$: any part of the defining union containing it would contain its whole image, hence the injective simplex on $F$, contradicting step 4. These two implications hold in every degree. By the horn definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], they give precisely the claimed intersection, with the inner index verified in step 3.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.8 proof, exact identification of the upper-left corner as the j-horn, in every simplicial degree. Printed pp.305-306 (PDF page indices 322-323), read online; archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Now $L_h=L_{h-1}\cup\Delta^T$. In each simplicial degree, the pushout of the two inclusions of the intersection is this union: the equivalence relation identifies exactly the two copies of the intersection, with no other identifications. Explicitly, maps $u:L_{h-1}\to X$ and $v:\Delta^d\to X$ agreeing on $\Lambda_a^d$ define a unique map from $L_h$ by $u$ on the first part and $v$ through the displayed face identification on the second. Step 5 makes this well-defined. Precomposition preserves each part, so the two simplicial naturality equations make the glued map simplicial. This proves the degreewise pushout assertion and its induced simplicial operators. Thus the filtration of step 2 has the required attachments, taking $d_h=d$ and $a_h=a$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.8 proof, displayed pushout square; its degreewise set gluing expanded explicitly. Printed pp.305-306 (PDF page indices 322-323), read online; archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: For a quasicategory $Q$ and the given map $f_0:K_J\to Q$, inductively suppose $f_{h-1}:L_{h-1}\to Q$ has been constructed. Restrict it along the attaching map $\Lambda_{a_h}^{d_h}\to L_{h-1}$. Since $0<a_h<d_h$, the defining horn-filling property of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives $g_h:\Delta^{d_h}\to Q$ whose restriction is exactly this map. The pushout established in step 6 glues $g_h$ and $f_{h-1}$ into $f_h:L_h\to Q$ with $f_h|_{L_{h-1}}=f_{h-1}$. Starting at $h=1$ and ending at the finite stage $t$ gives $f_t:\Delta^n\to Q$ with $f_t|_{K_J}=f_0$, as asserted.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.5.8, finite horn filtration; extension by the defining quasicategory horn fillers. Printed pp.305-306 (PDF page indices 322-323), read online; archival copy WANTED; no matching Stacks tag.
